Differential Calculus — Chain Rule

Chapter 2: Square Root of Exponential Function | Page 33

Home Work 26
Problem Statement Radical Exponential & Chain Rule
Find the derivative with respect to xxx of the function:
y=ex+1y = \sqrt{e^x + 1}y=ex+1​
STEP 1 প্রদত্ত সূচকীয় বর্গমূল ফাংশনটি ঘাত আকারে প্রকাশ করি (Expressing in Exponent Power Form)
y=(ex+1)1/2y = (e^x + 1)^{1/2}y=(ex+1)1/2
STEP 2 উভয়পক্ষে xxx-এর সাপেক্ষে অন্তরীকরণ অপারেটর প্রয়োগ করি (Applying Differentiation Operator w.r.t. x)
dydx=ddx[(ex+1)1/2]\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{d}{dx}\left[ (e^x + 1)^{1/2} \right]dxdy​=dxd​[(ex+1)1/2]
STEP 3 বহিঃস্থ সূচকের জন্য শক্তি বিধি (Power Rule) প্রয়োগ করি (Applying Power Rule to Outer Exponent)
dydx=12(ex+1)12−1⋅ddx(ex+1)=12(ex+1)−1/2⋅ddx(ex+1)\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2}(e^x + 1)^{\frac{1}{2} - 1} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}(e^x + 1) = \frac{1}{2}(e^x + 1)^{-1/2} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}(e^x + 1)dxdy​=21​(ex+1)21​−1⋅dxd​(ex+1)=21​(ex+1)−1/2⋅dxd​(ex+1)
STEP 4 অভ্যন্তরীণ সূচকীয় পদের অন্তরজ নির্ণয় করি (Differentiating Inner Exponential Expression)
ddx(ex+1)=ddx(ex)+ddx(1)=ex+0=ex\frac{d}{dx}(e^x + 1) = \frac{d}{dx}(e^x) + \frac{d}{dx}(1) = e^x + 0 = e^xdxd​(ex+1)=dxd​(ex)+dxd​(1)=ex+0=ex
STEP 5 মান প্রতিস্থাপন করে চূড়ান্ত সরল ভগ্নাংশ পাই (Substituting Derivative & Writing in Standard Radical Form)
dydx=12ex+1⋅ex=ex2ex+1\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{e^x + 1}} \cdot e^x = \frac{e^x}{2\sqrt{e^x + 1}}dxdy​=2ex+1​1​⋅ex=2ex+1​ex​
FINAL ANSWER dydx=ex2ex+1\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{e^x}{2\sqrt{e^x + 1}}dxdy​=2ex+1​ex​

📘 Box 1: Mathematical Foundations & Formula Reference
  • Standard Radical Derivative: ddx[u]=12ududx\frac{d}{dx}[\sqrt{u}] = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\frac{du}{dx}dxd​[u​]=2u​1​dxdu​.
  • Natural Exponential Derivative: ddx[ex]=ex\frac{d}{dx}[e^x] = e^xdxd​[ex]=ex.
  • Chain Rule Chain Composition: With u=ex+1u = e^x + 1u=ex+1, dydx=dydududx=12u⋅ex\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy}{du}\frac{du}{dx} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}} \cdot e^xdxdy​=dudy​dxdu​=2u​1​⋅ex.
⚠️ Box 2: Common Student Traps & Pitfalls
  • Radical Distribution Fallacy: Assuming ex+1=ex+1=ex/2+1\sqrt{e^x + 1} = \sqrt{e^x} + \sqrt{1} = e^{x/2} + 1ex+1​=ex​+1​=ex/2+1. Square roots never distribute over sums!
  • Missing Constant Derivative: Correctly recognising ddx(1)=0\frac{d}{dx}(1) = 0dxd​(1)=0, leaving solely exe^xex from the inner term.
  • Missing Coefficient 12\frac{1}{2}21​: Dropping the factor of 2 in the denominator during algebraic formatting.
🌐 Box 3: Real Domain & Differentiability Analysis
  • Domain of Definition: Since ex>0e^x > 0ex>0 for all real xxx, we have ex+1>1>0e^x + 1 > 1 > 0ex+1>1>0. The expression under the radical is strictly positive everywhere.
  • Strict Real Domain: Domain=(−∞,∞)=R\text{Domain} = (-\infty, \infty) = \mathbb{R}Domain=(−∞,∞)=R.
  • Smoothness: Infinitely differentiable (C∞C^\inftyC∞) everywhere on the real line.

  • Differentiating implicitly: 1ydydx=12⋅exex+1\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{e^x}{e^x + 1}y1​dxdy​=21​⋅ex+1ex​
  • Multiplying by y=ex+1y = \sqrt{e^x + 1}y=ex+1​: dydx=ex+1⋅ex2(ex+1)=ex2ex+1\frac{dy}{dx} = \sqrt{e^x + 1} \cdot \frac{e^x}{2(e^x + 1)} = \frac{e^x}{2\sqrt{e^x + 1}}dxdy​=ex+1​⋅2(ex+1)ex​=2ex+1​ex​
